scope: One defensive OAuth prerequisite for native PG REST/MCP authority; no database-domain wiring or approval
mechanism: One private OAuthService::lock_access_record helper, accessible to the existing nested MCP module, is shared by inspect_scoped, authorize_mcp_reference and revalidate_mcp_authority_in.

Discovery does not retain an access-row lock. For active discovery the helper locks issuer client, then native user/session, then the exact access row by id and stored token hash FOR SHARE. It reloads and compares id, token hash, issuer, subject and session. Missing/replaced/changed ownership returns None; database errors propagate.

Native initially missing access rows still reach the legacy JWT fallback when appropriate. A row lost after discovery returns inactive directly and cannot fall back to JWT or refresh introspection. Initially inactive discovery stays inactive, preserving conservative native inspection behavior.

MCP creates its server-owned reference from the current reloaded row and only returns it after existing claims, resource, role, scope and tenant-preview checks. Stored references discover using access id and hash without raw tokens, then compare the current record hash and existing issuer/subject/session/role/issued-at/expiry/write claims after the same helper.

Caller authentication/client locks remain in place. Resource relationship/policy locking remains in the existing validation path with deterministic issuer/caller resource grant ordering. No new early resource locks or access-first locks were introduced.

Existing McpGuard and caller-owned revalidation transactions retain the access/identity locks until their transaction ends. No new guard type, public inspector, wire field, authentication signature or generated ABI was introduced.

additiveAPI.trustBoundary: The getter never authorizes. A deserialized reference, including the parser fixtures, is untrusted until real revalidation; callers must retain the actual guard/transaction through their protected operation.

actualPureCoverage: Typed exact i64 expiry round-trip across minimum, negative, zero, ordinary timestamp and maximum values, preserving the existing camelCase wire shape and existing accessors. Parsing such values alone does not authenticate them.
Unexpected rawToken field, absent expiry and malformed null/string/fractional/out-of-range expiry values are rejected by the existing stored-reference parser.
Existing ordinary OAuth protocol/configuration/hash and BrowserSessions wire, origin/redirect and seal tests still pass.

method: Use the fixture's actual local-account/password-change/TOTP enrollment and confirmation, OAuth provisioning, consent, S256 PKCE and code exchange to obtain an MCP access token/reference.

For both MCP reference creation and stored-reference revalidation, hold the genuine native user row in a separate transaction and observe the verifier waiting using pg_blocking_pids. A separate exact access-row FOR UPDATE NOWAIT probe must still succeed while identity is blocked. All waits are bounded.
During the creation probe, commit a one-second-shorter expiry on the actual issued row before releasing identity; the returned reference getter must use this reloaded current expiry.

After stored-reference verification returns but before its transaction commits, an independent exact access-row NOWAIT probe must fail specifically with PostgreSQL 55P03 (lock_not_available); other database errors cannot count as success.
Keep the existing tampered-subject/expiry/refresh/replay checks and the existing initial-missing legacy JWT behavior coverage.
fixtureLimits: The existing fixture explicitly provisions an operator via create_local_account(..., true), marks its email verified with setup SQL, provisions signing/client records through existing offline APIs, and includes pre-existing role downgrade/restore and expiry mutation probes. It is not a clean HTTP signup/bootstrap acceptance proof.

It requires an owned retained-schema restricted localhost PostgreSQL fixture, privileged observer visibility, allocator capacity and separate connections. This session did not establish those prerequisites or execute it.
No synthetic session, operator role, Ready state or scope seed was added. New probes operate on the actual token issued by existing service flows.

No SQL-order RED/GREEN, reload race, retained-lock lifetime, disappeared/replaced-row, cross-client grant concurrency or live MCP/Database/native acceptance is claimed. Source review and a coordinated candidate fixture window remain necessary.
